update.title: Reduced XFCE forks while moving to 4.20
update.summary: Archived an unchanged clipboard-manager copy, rebased three focused panel patches onto XFCE 4.20, and retained the systemd-scope integration that still had no upstream equivalent.

blocks.body:
## Decide separately for each fork

I audited three XFCE components before moving the desktop to the 4.20 line. The clipboard manager matched upstream, so I archived it. The panel still required three changes: fixed pixel sizes for individual panel items, a configurable show-desktop button width, and crash fixes for pointer events during plugin removal. I rebased those changes onto XFCE 4.20. The `libxfce4ui` fork stayed because its systemd-scoped launcher had no upstream equivalent.

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  Audit[Audit each component] --> Difference{Local behavior still needed?}
  Difference -->|No| Archive[Archive unchanged copy]
  Difference -->|Focused patch set| Rebase[Rebase panel onto XFCE 4.20]
  Difference -->|No upstream equivalent| Retain[Keep systemd integration fork]
  Archive --> Verify[Verify migrated desktop session]
  Rebase --> Verify
  Retain --> Verify
blocks.description: The migration disposition followed the actual delta of each component rather than one fleet-wide rule.

blocks.body:
## Preserve the panel behavior on the new base

The custom panel loaded its complete plugin set and preserved the compact layout and 10-pixel show-desktop button after the rebase. The resulting maintenance boundary keeps only the deltas the desktop needs: three panel patches and one systemd integration fork.
